newsitem.title: UK: Green punt revalued under special EU arrangement.
newsitem.headline: Green punt revalued under special EU arrangement.

text.p: The green Irish punt was revalued on Friday, ahead of the normal schedule, after a special request by the Irish delegation to Thursday's EU cereals management committee, the UK Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said.

The green punt, which was undergoing the last of its five 10-day confirmation periods, was revalued to 0.812908 per Ecu in the agrimonetary grid from a previous rate of 0.829498. The change was decided on Thursday and effective on Friday.

HGCA officials said the decision to revalue the currency a day earlier was aimed at limiting the economic impact of the revaluation on Irish farmers. This is possible under Article 3.2 of the European Union (EU) Commission Regulations.
The currency was revalued only two percent, instead of three percent which would have been the case if the decision was made on Friday, effective from Monday.
The green punt remains in its last confirmation period for one more day but the risk for a second revaluation on the basis of Friday's exchange rates is considered to be tiny.
HGCA officials forecast no devaluations on Friday.
